segments.content:
Chapter 121: 0118 Xie Sao Bang is Here (Extra Chapter for Alliance Lord Zhe Xian Qi Tian)

Hangzhou Dianzi University, Xiasha Campus.

This campus was just opened last year, after a full three years of construction.

While Chen Guiliang was frantically skipping classes, Xie Yang was also skipping classes at Hangzhou Dianzi every day. This kid's number of failed courses might even be higher than Chen Guiliang's!

Xie Yang's life had been completely changed.

He had zero interest in his accounting major and spent all day at Tao Chenggang's "Bailian Network Technology Company." He worked part-time doing odd jobs at the company while learning programming from the experts there.

Tao Chenggang's company happened to be in Xiasha as well.

This was no coincidence; Xiasha was just a very remote location.

Office rent in Xiasha was the lowest, which was why Tao Chenggang had opened his company here. It was also the easiest place to acquire land, so Hangzhou Dianzi had built its new campus in this area.

"Damn, Xie Yang, you're skipping class again," a roommate exclaimed.

Xie Yang got on his bicycle. "Help me cover if they take attendance."

"Cover my ass. I got caught last week, and Professor Zhang gave me a lecture."

"Then just forget about it."

"You're definitely going to fail your courses like this."

"We'll see when the time comes."

Riding his bicycle, he sped off campus, heading straight for Tao Chenggang's company.

The Xiasha Economic Development Zone was currently in its early stages of development, with few commercial, dining, and other living facilities. It was also far from the main city area, making commuting very inconvenient.

To attract businesses, the office rent was less than a third of that in the main city, and it was easy to apply for the favorable policy of "three years free, two years half-price."

"Brother Gang!"

"Xiao Xie, you're so early? It's not my place to say, but you should still focus on your studies as a freshman."

"I don't want to study accounting. It's perfect to come here and learn programming from the experts."

"Sigh, suit yourself."

The expert Xie Yang mentioned was also one of the company's shareholders.

As Tao Chenggang continuously sold off his internet cafes and invested the money back into the company, his shares had made him the majority owner. The business was a huge money pit, and at most, Tao Chenggang could last another seven or eight months.

"Master, good morning."

"You're here."

Xie Yang could already handle some simple programming tasks.

For a period of time, the kid had practically lived at the company. Since he didn't have his own computer, he would use the company's computers at night to practice. He would sleep until noon, then get up and continue doing odd jobs, not going to school at all.

Not only would he fail his courses, but he might even have to repeat the year!

Seeing how obsessed he was, Tao Chenggang simply gave him a workstation.

Turning on the computer and logging into QQ, Xie Yang cracked his neck, ready to work.

There was a QQ message, Chen Guiliang's profile picture was flashing.

Xie Yang clicked on it and saw: "Xie Sao Bang, I've started a couple of companies. You can check them out when you're free. Here are the URLs. You need an invitation code to register on Xiaonei.com. Here's the code."

Xie Yang copied the URL and curiously went to Xiaonei.com.

He first used the invitation code to register an account, selected his region and school, and discovered he couldn't find a single classmate to add as a friend from his university.

He was the first user from Hangzhou Dianzi University on Xiaonei.com!

Looking at the homepage of Xiaonei, the most popular feature was the Campus Belle and Beau contest. You could click on it to view the details.

There was also a line of bold, red text on the homepage, which was about Sanguosha.

Upon entering, there was a detailed introduction to Sanguosha, and you could also jump to the official Sanguosha website to download the game.

Just as Xie Yang was downloading Sanguosha, Yang Yuhui walked up behind him and joked, "Slacking off?"

Yang Yuhui had also come to Hangzhou.

Tao Chenggang's internet cafes, game studio, and even "Legend of the Abyss" had all been sold off to raise funds.

"A game Chen Guiliang made," Xie Yang said, pointing to the download page.

Yang Yuhui was surprised. "He's making games too? And it's already launched?"

Xie Yang said, "It's still in open beta."

Yang Yuhui shouted to someone in the distance, "Brother Gang, come over here for a sec!"

Tao Chenggang walked over and asked, "What's up?"

"Chen Guiliang's game is online," Yang Yuhui said.

"That fast? Is it another Legend private server?" Tao Chenggang asked.

Xie Yang switched back to the Xiaonei homepage. "He's opened two companies, one for campus social networking and one for online games."

Tao Chenggang leaned over the computer, using the mouse to carefully look through everything. Finally, he sighed with emotion, "No wonder he refused to work with me. The guy had his own plans all along."

Yang Yuhui said, "A website like Xiaonei.com must be worth a lot, right?"

"I don't know. Venture capitalists would probably like it." Tao Chenggang wasn't very knowledgeable about this.

The dot-com bubble burst in 2000 and lasted until the end of 2002, with 90% of internet companies worldwide going bankrupt.

In 2003, just last year, the internet industry began to recover, but capital remained cautious.

In 2004, in August of this year, Google went public, raising 1.67 billion USD. This landmark event boosted market confidence, and capital became active again in the second half of the year.

This wave of internet investment fever wouldn't surge into China until next year.

At that time, investment firms from all over the world would be waving US dollars, searching for targets in China. They were rational at first, but gradually became frenzied, with many Chinese companies being severely overvalued. The venture capital firms were like fools throwing money around.

Chen Guiliang was about to catch this opportune moment.

So was Tao Chenggang. As long as he could hold on until next summer, it would be very easy for him to attract investment.

Xie Yang continued to download the game and browse Xiaonei.com, while the others returned to their workstations.

Once Sanguosha finished downloading, Xie Yang completed the newbie tutorial and started playing. He was a part-timer here, earning only five hundred yuan a month, so no one would bother him for playing games for a while.

As he played, he lost interest.

Xie Yang dropped the mouse and leaned back in his chair. He felt that this was all meaningless.

Especially his studies, which were a complete mess.

After thinking it over until noon, Xie Yang found Tao Chenggang. "Brother Gang, I don't want to work here anymore."

Tao Chenggang smiled. "You should have gone back to your studies a long time ago."

"I want to take a leave of absence from school and go to Beijing to find Chen Guiliang," Xie Yang said.

"Are you sure?" Tao Chenggang asked.

Xie Yang nodded. "I'm sure. I'm really not interested in accounting. I wanted to change my major two months ago. The school said I could, but there are restrictions, and I can't transfer to computer science. I don't want to study anymore, but it's hard to explain to my family, so I'll just take a year off."

"That's fine. Come back and visit when you have time," Tao Chenggang said, patting his shoulder.

Xie Yang said, "Thank you, Brother Gang, for taking care of me these past six months."

The procedure for taking a leave of absence went smoothly. The reason given was a family emergency that needed to be handled.

Universities at this time weren't very strict about such things.

Sister Furong, for example, took a leave of absence midway to go back and repeat her last year of high school to try for Tsinghua or Peking University. She ended up in a car accident during the college entrance exams and returned to university to continue her studies.

December 16th.

Dragging a worn-out suitcase, Xie Yang walked out of the Beijing Railway Station.

He took the wrong bus on his way to Peking University, and by the time he arrived at the south gate, it was already dark.

Xie Yang found a roadside phone booth, inserted a 201 phone card, and tried to call Chen Guiliang. Chen Guiliang had sent his new phone number to Xie Yang via QQ right after the school year started.

"Fuck!"

Xie Yang cursed in frustration. The phone screen displayed "Invalid Card."

201 phone cards from some regions could be used to make calls in other cities, but the one Xie Yang had couldn't.

He tried to find a public phone or a phone bar, but after searching around, he found none.

The weather was getting colder and colder. Xie Yang wandered aimlessly on the streets, not knowing where to go.

He had arranged with Chen Guiliang to call him upon arriving at Peking University, and they would meet outside the south gate.

Xie Yang asked for directions again and walked back to the south gate. Not daring to look at the security guard, he walked into the campus with a composed expression.

Luckily, this wasn't after 2008, or he wouldn't have been able to get in at all.

"It's snowing, it's snowing!"

Suddenly, the freshmen from the south began to cheer one after another.

The first snow of the winter in Beijing had finally begun to fall, as if to welcome Xie Yang's arrival.

Xie Yang stopped a student. "Excuse me, do you have a phone card? Can I borrow it to make a call? I can pay you."

The student thought for a moment, and instead of taking out a phone card, he directly took out his mobile phone. "Sure. Are you here to see a friend?"

"Yes, I'm looking for a high school classmate," Xie Yang said as he took the phone. "His name is Chen Guiliang, do you know him?"

The student immediately broke into a smile. "Of course I know him. We've even showered in the same public bathhouse. He lives in Building 36, I live in Building 37. We often run into each other when we get hot water or take a shower. Don't worry about the money. Just go to Building 36 and wait for him after you call."

"How do I get to Building 36?" Xie Yang asked.

The student said, "I'll take you. It's just a few hundred meters away."

The call connected. Xie Yang said, "Great Hero Chen, I'm at Peking University... Yeah, a kind student is taking me to Building 36."

Xie Yang handed the phone back to the student. "Is Chen Guiliang really famous at Peking University?"

"Extremely famous," the student said. "Especially after the campus belle and beau contest and the launch of Sanguosha, who among the students of Yanyuan doesn't know him?"

Xie Yang thought to himself: Great Hero Chen is truly Great Hero Chen. He did well at No. 2 High, and he's still doing well at Peking University. Why didn't I listen to his advice in my senior year? If I had just studied a bit harder back then, I could have gotten into a better university.

On the way, they passed several dormitories, and in the open spaces in front of the buildings, students were cheering about the snow.

In reality, the snow was falling very lightly.

When they arrived outside Building 36, many students were there as well, jumping around excitedly.

"Wu Meng!"

Xie Yang didn't see Chen Guiliang, but he recognized Wu Meng at a glance.

She was standing next to a row of bicycles with a roommate from the south, reaching out her hands to catch the snow drifting from the sky.

Wu Meng looked at Xie Yang with confusion, thinking her eyes were playing tricks on her, then she said with a delighted surprise, "Aren't you in Hangzhou? What are you doing at Peking University?"

Xie Yang smiled. "Couldn't make it there, so I came to seek refuge with my old classmate."

"Does Great Hero Chen know?" Wu Meng asked.

Xie Yang said, "I just called him. He said he's on his way."

Wu Meng asked again, "Have you eaten?"

"I've eaten." Xie Yang actually hadn't, but telling the truth would seem pathetic.

Wu Meng asked, "Are you planning to join Great Hero Chen's company?"

Xie Yang nodded. "I'll start by doing odd jobs and learn some things. I don't know anything right now."

"Ding-a-ling..."

The sound of a bicycle bell rang out as Chen Guiliang came racing over on his bike. "Didn't you say you'd arrive during the day?"

Xie Yang was a bit embarrassed. "I took the wrong bus. The public transport in Beijing is quite complicated."

"Let's go, I'll take you to get something to eat," Chen Guiliang said to Wu Meng. "Come with us. It'll be a reunion for us old classmates."

Wu Meng said, "Okay, I'm not full either."

Something came up, so this chapter is late.

(End of this chapter)
